text: By this test Shakespeare had already been approved. He had outlived his rivals and his patrons; and, when Johnson wrote, a century and a half, with its vicissitudes of taste, its new manners, and its new rules of writing, had passed upon his works without abating the delight which they afforded. Johnson comprises the event in one image (Johnson 1765): "The stream of time, which is continually washing the dissoluble fabricks of other poets, passes without injury by the adamant of Shakespeare."
